page: Amazon Web Services c9g.large is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family, utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs running at 3.3 GHz, with no hyperthreading. The memory configuration consists of 4.0 GB of RAM, yielding 2.0 GB per core. The instance operates on the Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core capabilities, with the Geekbench single-core score and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression tests achieving top-tier ratings. Conversely, multi-core performance is limited, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the weak category. Memory bandwidth is mixed, showing average performance for large block read operations but weak results for small block reads and large block writes.

The instance offers a resource-dense, cost-efficient profile for single-threaded tasks and lightweight compute workloads, avoiding the expense of larger multi-core configurations. However, the lack of local storage and the modest 4.0 GB memory capacity present clear tradeoffs for memory-intensive applications. It is best suited for single-threaded processing, text processing, lightweight static web serving, and basic database operations.
